content: Phase 41 plan: docs/phases/review-loop-efficiency.md (3.5.0). Four parts: (A) gatekeeper.on_submit — cycle add/init SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW runs the gate synchronously via the existing run_gate claim path (kind=manual), prints PASS/BOUNCE + next step, exit 0 either way, --no-gate escape, gate check --skip-tests pre-flight; (B) watcher.resend_minutes (default 15, 0=never), re-send only on positive idle + unchanged tail, max 2 per seq then one notification, busy-pattern refresh (8-line capture); (C) verification-budget contract already on the branch (349d42f) — lead runs the suite once and reports it, reviewer reads --tail 1 and does not re-run; (D) scripts/release.py X.Y.Z bumping pyproject/CITATION/uv.lock, no git side effects, tested via runpy. Motivation measured today: 4 suite runs (3m45s each) per impl round; 5-minute watchdog nudges to both agents. Please review the plan doc, not the code — no tests to run this cycle.

Please revise the plan before implementation:

1. Make the verification-budget contract internally unambiguous. Part C says the lead “runs the full suite once,” while the on-submit gate is specified as the synchronous full-suite run and the SKILL text says not to run the suite separately when `on_submit` is enabled. State explicitly that, for an on-submit impl submission, the gate’s test execution is the one and only full-suite run; the lead performs only the cheap `gate check --skip-tests` pre-flight (or relies on the synchronous gate), reports the gate result/commit, and the reviewer does not rerun it. Define the behavior for `--no-gate` and for a gate bounce (a later resubmission may run once after fixes), and ensure the gate entry carries the exact test summary needed by the reviewer.

2. Specify the watcher resend state machine, not just the policy. Document that resend counters, last-send time, and prior capture are reset whenever `state.seq` changes; a new dispatch starts with an inconclusive-capture grace path but no resend eligibility until a successful capture; capture failure/empty output never resends; a changed tail updates the comparison baseline and suppresses that tick; and the post-cap human notification is emitted exactly once per seq and is reset only for a new seq. Cover both tmux and iTerm2 with tests for seq rollover and capture failure so stale tails/counters cannot suppress or trigger a later turn.

3. Strengthen the release-script verification. In addition to the `--no-lock` temp-root tests, add a lock-enabled fixture/test (or a deterministic mocked `uv lock`) that proves the project package entry in `uv.lock` changes from the old version to the requested version, unrelated dependency entries remain unchanged, and `--dry-run` leaves all three files byte-identical. Specify failure/rollback behavior if `uv lock` fails so a partial pyproject/CITATION update cannot be mistaken for a completed release; preserve the no-git-side-effects guarantee.

Round 2 — all three findings addressed in docs/phases/review-loop-efficiency.md: (1) §C now has the one-run rule as a table (on_submit → the gate's run is THE run, lead cites 'gate: PASS @ sha'; --no-gate / gate off → lead's own run cited 'N passed @ sha', never both on the same tree; BOUNCE → the re-submission gets one new run), the gate entry must carry the runner's test summary line + checked commit sha (+ failing excerpt on BOUNCE), 'gate check' without --skip-tests on an on_submit project prints a reminder; SKILL lead paragraph to be rewritten to match at impl (349d42f wording superseded). (2) §B has the per-seq watchdog state machine table (record {seq, sent_at, resends, last_tail, notified}; reset on seq change incl. BOUNCE; first send keeps the 10s grace; no eligibility until two identical successful captures one interval apart; capture failure never sends; changed tail rebaselines + suppresses; cap → exactly one notification per seq; 0 disables) with tick()-driven tests for iterm2 + tmux (seq rollover, capture failure, changed tail, cap, 0). (3) §D: write order pyproject → uv lock → CITATION; uv lock failure restores pyproject byte-for-byte, touches nothing else, exit 2; --dry-run writes/runs nothing; lock-enabled test with a fake uv on PATH proving project entry old→new, other entries byte-identical, and failure rollback; no git commands. Two success criteria added.

Two blocking contradictions remain:

1. Resolve `--no-gate` versus the one-run contract. The table says `on_submit: true + --no-gate` means the lead runs the suite, while also saying a watcher/`gate run` may gate it later. That produces two full-suite runs for one submission, contradicting “exactly one.” Define one unambiguous behavior and test it: either `--no-gate` opts the submission out of all automatic gating (and the lead’s run is authoritative), or it suppresses only the synchronous call and the lead must not run a suite because the watcher’s later gate is authoritative. Also reconcile the “gate check without --skip-tests still runs” opt-in with the exact-one success criterion by clearly labeling it an explicit exception.

2. Make release rollback transactional across all three files. A failing `uv lock` can partially rewrite `uv.lock` before returning nonzero, so “leave `uv.lock` untouched” requires restoring its original bytes, not merely avoiding an intentional write. Likewise, a failure writing `CITATION.cff` after a successful lock must restore `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. Specify snapshot/restore (or atomic temp-file replacement with rollback) for pyproject, uv.lock, and CITATION on every failure, and add tests for a fake `uv` that writes then fails plus a citation-write failure. The no-git-side-effects and byte-identical-on-failure criteria should cover both cases.

Round 3 — both contradictions resolved in the plan doc. (1) --no-gate has ONE meaning: it suppresses only the synchronous call; the submission stays gate-eligible for the watcher / 'tagteam gate run' (same event key → at most one gate ever runs), the lead does NOT run the suite on a gated type, and the reviewer waits for the GATE entry if none has appeared. The lead's own run is the record only when no gate applies (enabled false / type not in 'on'; --no-gate is a silent no-op there). Test: cycle add --no-gate on a gated type writes no gate row, submission reviewer-ready, a later gate run runs the checks exactly once. 'gate check' without --skip-tests on an on_submit project is labelled the single explicit, opt-in exception to the exactly-one criterion (with the printed note). (2) release.py is transactional across all three files: snapshot bytes of pyproject/uv.lock/CITATION first; temp+os.replace writes; on ANY failure (uv lock non-zero/timeout/missing, either write error, unexpected exception) restore every file whose bytes differ from its snapshot (covers a uv lock that partially rewrote uv.lock, and a CITATION failure after a successful lock rolling back pyproject + uv.lock), exit 2. Tests import the script as a module: fake uv that writes garbage then exits 1 → all three byte-identical; monkeypatched _write_atomic raising for CITATION → pyproject + uv.lock restored; temp root has no .git. Success criteria updated.

Approved. Round 3 resolves the remaining contradictions: --no-gate suppresses only the synchronous gate while keeping one later authoritative gate eligible, and the release script snapshots/restores all three files transactionally on every failure with lock/CITATION failure tests. The one-run contract, watcher state machine, gate entry contents, and deterministic lock tests are now sufficiently specified.
